messages:
Alex W: fyi dashboards flagged a p95/p99 surge on hosted-api at ~09:12 UTC. p95 from ~210ms -> ~760ms for ~15m, queue depth high on a few hosts.

sre-bot: alert: hosted-api latency_p95 > 500ms for 2024-10-18T09:12:00Z region=us-west-2 route=/v1/generate

Maria L: jumping in — traces show lots of kernel selector churn. several hosts flipping between `main` and `aux` rapidly.

Raj S: pulling quick host snapshot for suspected hotspot (host=gpu-23):
```
queue_depth=48
avg_batch_size=2.8
kselector.switches.last_30m=112
kv_cache.hit_rate=0.87
eviction_rate=0.33/s
gpu_util=78%
```

Tina P: tenant-level kv-cache metrics show a small shard getting hammered, eviction_rate jumped ~3x at the same time as the kselector flips.

Alex W: my initial hunch: recent kselector heuristic change lowered coalesce threshold -> more short batches -> aux kernel chosen more often -> aux path does heavier prefetch/serialize -> hot-shard thrash -> queue backs up -> latency spike. likely noisy tenant causing lots of short-seq requests.

Maria L: heres a brief timeline from runtime logs:
```
09:11:38 scheduler wait +10ms
09:11:40 kselector: main->aux
09:11:41 kselector: aux->main
09:11:43 prefetch: cache_miss_burst
09:11:45 batcher: flush_short_batches
```

Raj S: noticed rate limiter for that shard hit ~95% token cap briefly. microbursting + hard cap can cause downstream scheduling jitter.

Tina P: I captured a flamegraph for aux path: `kv_prefetch` and `serialize_batch` dominate. aux uses a different layout and issues more prefetch requests which makes a hot keyshard worse.

Alex W: any deploys/rollouts around 09:00?

deploy-bot: deploy: branch=runtime/kselector-tuned commit=ad3f9c3 user=maria.l started=2024-10-18T08:53:12Z finished=2024-10-18T08:54:05Z rollout=10%->100% by 09:05

Maria L: correct — that rollout changed the short-seq coalescing threshold (intended to reduce tail for small requests). seems to have increased small-batch incidence for some workloads.

Raj S: mitigation options:
- revert the kselector heuristic (revert commit ad3f9c3) on affected pool(s)
- pin noisy tenant(s) to `main` kernel variant

Tina P: I pinned tenant XYZ to `main` on gpu-23/gpu-24 as an emergency measure. queue depth on those hosts dropped 48 -> 6 within ~40s, p95 moving back toward baseline.

Alex W: great. action items to follow up:
- Maria L: open revert PR + AB test (owner: Maria) [IN PROGRESS]
- Raj S: add smoothing to ratecap to avoid microburst gating (owner: Raj)
- Tina P: add kv-cache shard hotness alert + kernel-pin runbook (owner: Tina)
- Alex W / SRE: scan other pools for kselector churn (owner: Alex)

Maria L: creating PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/442 (revert ad3f9c3 + perf regression tests). adding synthetic mixed-short/long sequence test.

Raj S: applying short-term smoothing config to rate engine for the hostpool we saw the spike on. will monitor metrics.

sre-bot: incident recorded: #INC-2024-561 latency spike. postmortem milestone assigned.

Alex W: TL;DR: kselector tweak unintentionally amplified noisy-tenant short-batch pattern via aux-path prefetchs -> hot shard eviction thrash -> queue buildup. Good mitigation path: kernel pin + revert + smoother ratecap + alerts/tests.

Tina P: I'll write the runbook snippet for on-call: detection (kselector.switches.rate + kv_cache.eviction_rate), how to pin tenant, and rollback steps.

Maria L: PR will include a regression harness that simulates high short-seq ratio and asserts kselector.switches < threshold.

Raj S: monitoring follow-up: add alert when kselector.switches.rate > 30/min AND kv_cache.eviction_rate > 2x baseline within 5m.

Alex W: nice work everyone. mark this thread resolved once PR merges and runbook/alert are in place :thumbsup:
